data.hypothesis: The three prior scalar schedules were correct but slower than the 55.00 µs baseline: two groups measured 82.32 µs, three groups 147.64 µs, and four groups 63.81 µs. The catalog reports three distinct prior programs. This eight-group (64-input-character) schedule tests whether more independent scalar table-lookup chains and less loop control can improve on the four-group candidate; its larger live-value set and code footprint may instead hurt. No speedup is assumed.
data.notes: The unsuccessful measured choices remain relevant: two-, three-, and four-group schedules were all slower than baseline, with four groups the best of those candidates. This proposal uses a contrasting eight-group factor, not benchmark-length specialization. No commands or measurements were run here; the controller should validate empty/short inputs, group-boundary lengths, padding cases, random valid inputs, and Lena, then perform repeated native timing before judging it.
transformations: Added a scalar helper that performs all eight table lookups for an eight-character word without early branching and records validity separately.
Unrolled the decode loop to load and decode eight independent eight-character words per iteration, delaying the combined validity decision until all eight results are computed.
Required at least 69 remaining input characters before consuming 64, preserving the existing scalar decoder for invalid input, padding, and tails.
Added no explicit SIMD, parallel execution, benchmark-size specialization, or changes outside src/candidate.cpp.
